title: Hanging pieces
objectives: Recognize when a piece is attacked and undefended

steps.text: A piece is "hanging" when it's attacked and nothing defends it. Leave a hanging piece where it is, and your opponent captures it for free — before you move, always check whether the square you're leaving a piece on (or moving it to) is actually defended.

hints.text: One of Black's pieces has no defender at all — find it.
Your rook already lines up with the undefended knight.
Rxd4 wins the knight — nothing was defending it.

feedback.default: That doesn't win any material. Which black piece is attacked and has no defender at all?

steps.successExplanation: Rxd4 wins the knight for free — nothing defended it.

steps.prompt: Your knight attacks an enemy bishop, but the bishop is also defended by their queen. What does that mean?
options: The bishop is hanging — capture it for free
The bishop is defended — capturing it starts a trade, not a free win
You should never capture a defended piece
The bishop can't be captured at all

feedback.default: A defended piece isn't hanging. Capturing it just trades your piece for theirs — worth doing sometimes, but it's not free material.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a defended piece isn't "hanging." Capturing it just trades your piece for theirs, not a free win.

steps.summary: A hanging piece is attacked and undefended — check both before deciding a piece, yours or theirs, is actually safe.
